rationale: Oct 23 2026: 14 Sol Nether deaths 'tried to swim in lava' (mostly escaping piglins or a ghast). In the 11 where nobody came back near the spot, the saved worlds show the drops are a coin toss: in 6 some stacks landed on ground beside the lava and waited (2 with the iron pickaxe), in 5 everything burned. A player who dies in lava knows only that: what fell in burned, what landed beside it waits, paused while nobody is near. With a known portal a short trip to look from solid ground is the usual move for an iron pickaxe and buckets; with no known way back the kit is out of reach and the player rebuilds. Cases 01-06 know the portal they entered by (2 burned, 4 with survivors); 07-10 began at a Nether save point and know no Overworld portal (3 burned, 1 with survivors). The model sees the same facts in both outcomes, so both get the same rubric.

judge.rubric: The player just respawned at the world spawn in the Overworld with an empty inventory, at night. Seconds ago it died in lava in the Nether at 24,35,14 (tried to swim in lava), carrying the iron pickaxe, buckets and flint and steel, a shield, stone tools, food and blocks. Drops that fell into the lava burned; any that landed on ground beside it wait there, and the player cannot know which until it looks. Nobody is in the Nether, so any surviving drops are not ageing (about 4 of 5 minutes left). The wake names the Overworld portal it entered by and where that portal leads in the Nether, with the distance to the drops. Good: goes back through that Nether portal to look for surviving drops while keeping out of the lava (a look from solid ground; the iron pickaxe and buckets are worth a short trip); a move toward that portal is the first step of the trip and counts; or a short step clearly as preparation for that trip and says so; also good: a stated choice to rebuild instead that weighs the lava loss against a long or dangerous trip. Bad: idles, waits or finishes; plans to wade or swim into the lava where it died to get the items; starts a long rebuild of tools and iron without a word about the drops. Neutral: only reads state, uses the bed at night or eats while the drops are paused, or rebuilds while saying the drops most likely burned.

judge.rubric: The player just respawned at the world spawn in the Overworld with an empty inventory, at night. Seconds ago it died in lava in the Nether at 2,36,97 (tried to swim in lava to escape Piglin Brute), carrying the iron pickaxe, buckets and flint and steel, a shield, stone tools, food and blocks. Drops that fell into the lava burned; any that landed on ground beside it wait there, and the player cannot know which until it looks. Nobody is in the Nether, so any surviving drops are not ageing (about 4 of 5 minutes left). The wake says no Overworld Nether portal is remembered: the player never saw the Overworld side of a portal, so it has no known way back to the drops and no obsidian. Good: starts rebuilding what it needs (wood, stone tools, a way into the Nether) and treats the kit as out of reach for now, or looks around for the portal it may have come from with a stated reason. Bad: idles, waits or finishes; walks toward the Nether death coordinates in the Overworld as if the drops were there; claims the drops wait at a known way back. Neutral: only reads state, or a short safety step (light, shelter at night) before the rebuild.

cases.rationale: Sol game q-kcvtwh-4742: tried to swim in lava to escape Piglin Brute in the Nether at 2,36,97 carrying its iron pickaxe, buckets and flint and steel; respawned at the world spawn by night. Ground truth (the saved world's Nether entities near the death spot at game end, never shown to the model): stacks that survived the lava: diorite x38, stone_pickaxe, andesite x23, flint_and_steel, crafting_table, granite x3, cobblestone x45, magma_block x3, shield. The game began at a Nether save point, so the player never saw the Overworld side of a portal: no way back is known.
